key_insight: A heterogeneous CPU–GPU finite element framework accelerates tetrahedral-mesh micromagnetic simulations by targeting demagnetization-field evaluation and sparse linear solves.
engineering_relevance: Faster repeated micromagnetic simulations can support the design and evaluation of magnetic storage materials.
method: Extend the existing AFEMAG solver with heterogeneous CPU–GPU execution.
Offload computationally intensive boundary integral evaluations and sparse linear solves to the GPU.
Retain assembly and iteration control on the CPU.
evidence_signal: Validation covers all five μMag standard problems, with a reported 17.1× speedup for Standard Problem 3 on 137,313 nodes using one NVIDIA A100 versus the CPU-only configuration.
watch_item: The reported peak speedup is hardware- and case-specific; performance on other GPUs and mesh sizes requires evaluation.
paper_title: A Heterogeneous CPU-GPU Framework for Finite Element Micromagnetic Simulations on Tetrahedral Meshes
